$comment: See host.schema.json's own $comment for why every field lives inside the `container:` object, name included. image/size are required only when there is no `extends`.

container.description: A container: the same idea as a host, but deployed as a container instead of a VM. Every builder supports this -- natively where the hoster has a container primitive, by running the image on a small host otherwise -- and an author never chooses which. Lives in `hosts/` alongside hosts, sharing one name namespace with them.

name.description: Unique name for this container, referenced from an environment's topology and from other objects' `depends_on`. Not a hostname -- the environment's `as` field on each copy sets the actual hostname.

image.description: The OCI image ref to run, e.g. "nginx:alpine" or "registry.internal/team/scoreboard:latest". Pulled from Docker Hub, or from a configured private registry when the ref names one. Run as a container by whatever primitive the builder has (native OCI, or a nested runtime) -- you never pick the runtime.

size.description: Abstract size name (e.g. "small", "medium", "large"). Each builder config maps this to concrete CPU/memory for its hoster.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the container.

command.description: Overrides the image's default command arguments.

ports.description: TCP/UDP ports this container listens on.

depends_on.description: Other hosts, containers, or networks that must be up before this container builds. Names the object, not one specific copy: every copy of that object within the same team is waited on. This container's own network is always waited on implicitly.

steps.description: The ordered steps this container runs after it's provisioned. Each one is exactly one of the action kinds below, plus an optional `validate` block. They run INSIDE the container (its agent is the container's entrypoint on every builder), so they describe the application itself -- not the container runtime underneath it: a check like `process_running: nginx` or `port_listening: 80` is right, `process_running: dockerd` is not. For anything recurring or time-based, use `schedule:` instead -- steps run once, in order; they were never meant to hold recurring work.

schedule.description: Recurring or anchor-relative triggers for this container, independent of `steps:`'s own order -- each entry fires on its own clock, per its `when:`.
schedule.example:
schedule:
  - when: Every 30 minutes
    script: reboot
  - when: 30 minutes before access closes
    run: systemctl restart nginx

vars.description: Key/value data available to this container's own scripts, on top of whatever cascades down from its environment and network.

tags.description: Labels for searching, grouping, and ad-hoc targeting.

findings.description: Findings that belong to this container specifically.
findings.example:
findings:
  - severity: 4
    difficulty: 2
    description: SQL injection in the login form

extends.description: Name of another container this one extends. The base is deep-merged in: scalar fields (image/size) the child sets win, otherwise they're inherited; env/vars/tags merge key-by-key (child wins a clash); steps, people, command and ports are the base's followed by the child's. `image`/`size` become optional here since they're inherited.
